title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem: Definition: Which of these best defines a workflow, as the term is used for systems built on language models?

options.text: A system that sends the model one prompt per request and returns its reply with no further steps
A system where the program's code fixes the sequence of model calls and tools in advance
A system in which the model is given tools but a person approves every call
A system that uses the model for one narrow job, such as labelling a message, and nothing else

items.stem: Definition: Which of these best defines an agent?

options.text: A system that calls the model several times per request, with each call's prompt written by the team
A system in which the model is given a detailed prompt that lists every step to follow
A system where the model dynamically directs its own steps and tool use
A system whose code hands the model a tool at one stage of a longer pipeline

items.stem: Definition: In one phrase, what does "control flow" mean for a system built on a language model?
Definition: Which of these best defines prompt chaining?

options.text: Splitting a task into stages where each model call works on the previous call's output
Sending one input to several model calls at the same time and merging all their outputs
Having the model call itself repeatedly until it decides the task is done
Letting a person review each model output before the next call is made

items.stem: Definition: In one sentence, what does a routing workflow do with an incoming request?

Applying it: Your makerspace assistant receives "How do I change the nozzle on the Prusa printer?" The program text reads: results = search_manuals(question); reply = model(question, results); print(reply). Is this a workflow or an agent, and why?

options.text: An agent, because the model writes the reply that the student finally reads on the screen
An agent, because the search results change what the model writes in its reply
A workflow, because the program text already settles what runs first and what runs second
A workflow, because the model is called only once

items.stem: Applying it: Which part of the makerspace assistant is the strongest candidate for a fixed workflow rather than an agent?

options.text: Diagnosing why a student's 3D prints keep warping and suggesting what to change
Booking a machine slot for a trained student when the calendar shows the slot is free
Helping a student plan a project that needs both the laser cutter and the 3D printer
Responding when a student reports a machine fault that the manual does not mention

items.stem: Applying it: The sponsor allows $0.05 per request in expected cost, not worst-case cost. Design W is a fixed workflow: always 3 model calls per request, each with 1,500 input tokens and 300 output tokens. Design A is an agent: on average 5 model calls per request (at most 8), each with 3,000 input tokens and 300 output tokens. A token is a small chunk of text; the price is $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens. Exactly one design exceeds the allowance on expected cost. By how many dollars per request does it exceed it?

Applying it: Booking can be built as a fixed workflow or as an agent, and both book correctly. In one sentence, name one reason a reviewer should accept for choosing the workflow, and say what about fixed steps causes it.

Applying it: A team proposes this design for open questions such as "Can I build my project on the laser cutter this week?" Step 1: code checks the student's training record and stops if training is missing. Step 2: the model, given search_manuals and check_calendar tools, may make up to 6 calls to work out an answer. Step 3: code saves the answer to a log. Which statement about who decides what happens next is accurate?

options.text: The model decides at all three steps, because it is the only part that calls tools
Code decides at steps 1 and 3; the model decides which lookups happen in step 2 and when it stops
Code decides at all three steps, because it sets the six-call limit
The model decides at step 2 only whether to stop; the code decides which tool each of the six calls uses, in a set order
